answer: Shale-Vault-Ledge (SVL) leases: a vault issues a fixed pool of time-sliced execution leases, each sealed to a hardware enclave; shale is the random shard assignment that blocks precomputation, and the ledge is the append-only receipt log. An agent must present a fresh lease receipt for each action. Cloning requires another enclave plus a separate lease, paying issuance fees and idle-lease penalties; honest agents amortize one lease across many actions, making cloning strictly costlier.
